rows.question: For the retail sales area, what if we lower just a quarter of the ceiling to 7 feet for ductwork and leave the rest at 7 feet 6 inches?
rows.deliveredAnswerText:
Yes, conditionally—the proposed heights satisfy the furred-ceiling rule if the retail sales area is governed by the occupiable-space minimum and the lowered ceiling qualifies as a furred ceiling. Otherwise, the 7-foot portion fails the ordinary 7-foot-6-inch occupiable-space minimum; if the area is habitable, both proposed heights fall below its 8-foot minimum. (BC §§ 1208.2, 1208.2.1)

For a furred ceiling, the applicable minimum must be maintained over at least two-thirds of the room, with no furred-ceiling portion below 7 feet. Your arrangement leaves 3/4 = 75% at 7 feet 6 inches—more than two-thirds—and the lowered quarter meets the 7-foot floor. The higher portion meets, rather than exceeds, the occupiable-space minimum. The habitable-space exception instead requires the minimum established in § 1208.2. Measure all heights from the finished floor to the finished underside of the ceiling or ceiling beams. (BC §§ 1208.2, 1208.2.1)

The supplied text does not define “habitable” or “occupiable” sufficiently to resolve the retail-area classification, or “furred ceiling” sufficiently to classify the proposed ductwork enclosure. Thus this is a conditional ceiling-height result, not an unconditional approval.

rows.question: For a gas boiler in the proposed building, can we run steel gas piping outdoors along the rear wall? What protection should the detail show?
rows.deliveredAnswerText:
Yes—an exposed steel gas-piping run outdoors along the rear wall is permitted under the supplied 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code outdoor-piping rule, subject to its installation conditions. It must remain unconcealed and at least 3½ inches above ground. (FGC § 404.9)

The detail should show:

Corrosion protection: galvanizing, bonded coating complying with § 404.11.4, protective coating complying with § 404.11.5, or protective wrapping complying with § 404.11.6. Wrapping must be approved for the application and field-applied according to the manufacturer’s instructions. The supplied evidence does not include the specifications in §§ 404.11.4–404.11.5, so a particular bonded or protective coating cannot be approved from this packet. (FGC §§ 404.11.2, 404.11.6)
Identification: yellow labels marked “Gas” in black letters, complying with ASME A13.1, at intervals not exceeding 5 feet; where a gas test is required, labeling must be completed before that test. (FGC § 401.5)
Wall penetration, if provided: corrosion protection where the pipe passes through the outside wall. If encased in a protective pipe sleeve, seal the annular space and provide at least one end with a vented outlet piped to a safe outdoor location. The vent terminal must be at least 18 inches above grade, not under a building opening or overhang, and arranged to prevent entry of water and insects. (FGC § 404.9)

The support and physical-damage-protection sentence in § 404.9 applies to piping installed above ground, outdoors, and across roof surfaces; it does not establish those requirements for this rear-wall run.
rows.operativeConclusionReview: A qualified outdoor-piping/detail baseline is supplied, not full routing approval. Ground clearance, exposure, corrosion methods, labels and conditional penetration/sleeve vent details are accurate. No particular coating was proposed yet, so unavailable detailed coating specifications do not prevent this requested baseline.

sourceClauseReasons.reason: Outdoor piping at least 3½ inches above ground; no concealment; roof clearance separately scoped. Conditional exterior-wall corrosion and protective-sleeve sealed annular space/safe vent with 18-inch grade clearance and opening/overhang/water/insect controls are accurate. The support/physical-damage sentence has conjunctive outdoor, above-ground and roof-surface scope; it does not by itself establish those wall-only requirements.
Approved corrosion protection for susceptible metal; all four exterior-ferrous methods retained: galvanizing, bonded coatings, protective coatings, protective wrapping.
Wrapping is approved for the application and field-applied under manufacturer instructions.
Yellow Gas labels, black letters, ASME A13.1, spacing at most 5 feet and completion before a required gas test are accurate. The same-appliance-room exception does not describe this outdoor wall run.

rows.question: Could a café tenant keep propane cylinders outside this building? What fire-safety restrictions should we check before drawing a storage cage?
rows.deliveredAnswerText:
Possibly, but larger cylinders on this proposed residential mixed-use lot require Fire Commissioner authorization—not merely a compliant cage. On any lot containing a building used for residential occupancy, LPG containers with capacity greater than 16.4 ounces are prohibited unless authorized by the commissioner. Outdoor LPG storage also requires approval. The proposed residential use therefore matters even though the cylinders would serve a café outside the building. (FC §§ 6105.3, 6109.1)

Before drawing the cage, check:

Quantity and location: Outdoor storage is limited to 400 pounds of LPG, at or above grade; individual containers may not exceed 100 pounds capacity. Storage is prohibited on roofs and below grade under FC 6109. (FC §§ 6105.3, 6109.6–6109.7, 6109.12)
Baseline clearances: Maintain at least 20 feet from building openings, 20 feet from motor-vehicle fuel dispensers, and 10 feet from combustible material. These requirements include containers connected for use. (FC § 6109.12)
Additional exposure distances: For storage over 100 pounds through 400 pounds, Table 6109.12 requires, among other distances, 25 feet from subway openings and Group A occupancies/public gathering places; 10 feet from combustible-construction buildings, public sidewalks, parked vehicles, public streets, private roads and lot lines; and 5 feet from air-compressor intakes or heating, ventilation or air-conditioning inlets. Nearby liquid, gas, oxygen and solid-material storage must also be checked against its specific table row. Only entries marked footnote “a” allow reduction to 5 feet: a protective structure rated at least 2 hours must interrupt the line of sight, stand at least 5 feet from the exposure, and allow natural ventilation to prevent hazardous gas accumulation. That reduction does not apply to the unmarked subway or public-gathering rows. (FC Table 6109.12)
Cylinder positioning and valves: Stored containers with individual capacity greater than 1 pound must have their pressure-relief valve in direct communication with the container’s vapor space. Secure screw-on valve caps or collars on full, partially full and empty containers, and keep outlet valves closed. (FC §§ 6109.3, 6109.8)
Enclosure, damage and egress: Provide a suitable enclosure or other protection against tampering, plus vehicular protection as required by the commissioner. Locate cylinders to minimize physical damage, tampering and excessive temperature rise. Do not store or leave them unattended near exit-access doors, exits, stairs, exit-discharge areas or other means of egress. (FC §§ 6109.2, 6109.4, 6109.13)
Utility hazards and electrical equipment: Avoid locations where failure of electric power lines or piping carrying flammable/combustible liquids, flammable gases or oxidizing materials would expose the LPG to those hazards. Except as otherwise provided in NFPA 58, electrical equipment within 3 feet in any direction must meet Class I, Division 2 wiring requirements unless separated by a wall or solid partition with no openings. (FC §§ 6109.12.1, 6109.14)

If the cylinders would supply a stationary installation, availability of public-utility piped natural gas is another restriction: such LPG installations are prohibited where that access is available unless authorized by the commissioner. (FC § 6105.3)

Cylinder capacities, total LPG quantity, the proposed location and exposure distances, and commissioner authorization remain unresolved. The supplied packet lacks FC § 105.6’s permit thresholds, so it does not settle whether a separate permit is required. It also lacks the referenced NFPA 58 exception text, so no electrical exception beyond the stated solid-partition alternative can be evaluated here.

What cylinder capacities and total pounds of LPG does the café propose to keep outside?
rows.operativeConclusionReview: The initial answer correctly leads with the greater-than-16.4-ounce residential-lot restriction and commissioner authorization, does not turn retail use or an otherwise compliant cage into permission, and supplies conditional outdoor-storage safeguards. Every extra numerical/table/electrical statement was independently checked against full FC 6109, not accepted from verifier status.

sourceClauseReasons.reason: Maximum individual capacity, approval, separate permit threshold dependency, residential-lot greater-than-16.4-ounce prohibition/commissioner authorization, and stationary-installation utility-natural-gas restriction are correctly qualified. Approval and damage/tampering/temperature/egress safeguards, over-one-pound vapor-space relief-valve position, roof/below-grade storage restrictions, caps/collars/closed valves, enclosure and commissioner vehicular protection match canonical text. Never-LPG-container and construction-site exceptions are not stated premises.

400-pound outdoor maximum/at-or-above-grade; 20-foot openings and fuel-dispenser, 10-foot combustible baseline; more-than-100-through-400-pound table band and all quoted distances checked. Only marked rows receive the 5-foot, 2-hour line-of-sight protective-structure alternative with 5-foot exposure separation and natural ventilation. rows.question: The old property record shows zero apartments. Can we use that to say no residential parking is needed for the new building?
rows.deliveredAnswerText:
No—the old record’s zero apartments describes the existing property, not the proposed new building, and does not establish that no residential parking is needed. ZR § 25-212 calculates parking required to be maintained for existing multiple-dwelling residences under § 25-211; its pre-December 5, 2024 unit count is not a substitute for applying the rule governing new apartments.

The supplied current rule does establish that, in the indicated districts within the Inner Transit Zone, dwelling units or rooming units created after December 5, 2024 require no accessory off-street parking. “Created” means issuance of a temporary certificate of occupancy—or a final certificate if no temporary certificate was issued. (ZR § 25-211) That could provide a separate basis for no residential parking, but this packet cannot establish its geographic applicability: your stated Appendix I transit-zone location is accepted as a premise, while the supplied § 12-10 text says only “see Transit Zone, Inner” and omits the operative definition connecting that premise to the Inner Transit Zone.

The answer neither grants an unsupported Inner exemption nor affirmatively misclassifies the lot; missing Outer applicability/rate/waiver continuation is a minor issue relative to the specific inventory-inference question, consistent with original v19 rubric.

additionalCanonicalSourceChecks.text: All piping installed in new construction and all new piping installed in existing buildings, whether or not the piping is intended to be enclosed when construction is completed, shall be identified by a yellow label marked "Gas" in black letters. Where the installation requires a gas test such labeling shall be completed prior to such test. Labels shall be provided in accordance with ASME A13.1 and the marking shall be spaced at intervals not exceeding 5 feet (1524 mm). The marking shall not be required on pipe located in the same room as the appliance served.

Pipe protective bonded coatings shall be approved for the application and shall be factory applied. Exception: Where installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions, field application of bonded coatings shall be permitted for pipe, fittings and locations where the factory coating or wrapping has been damaged or necessarily removed at joints.
Pipe protective wrappings shall be approved for the application and shall be field applied in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.

Piping shall be provided with support in accordance with Section 407.2. In addition, when earthquake loads are applicable in accordance with the New York City Building Code, a detailed piping system stress analysis including seismic analysis shall be performed. The pipe supports and restraints shall be designed and installed to accommodate the resultant seismic forces, moments and displacements from this stress analysis in accordance with the New York City Building Code.
